newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Nearly one third of South Africans unemployed - CSS.
newsitem.headline: Nearly one third of South Africans unemployed - CSS.

text.p: Nearly a third of South Africa's economically active population is unemployed, according to results of a survey released by the Central Statistical Service (CSS) on Friday.
The CSS said in its October Household Survey that 29.3 percent of the country's estimated 41.5 million people over the age of 15 who had the desire to work were unemployed.

Of the total number of unemployed, 47 percent were black women, while black men accounted for 29 percent. White men represented just four percent of total unemployment in the country last year and white women eight percent.
Three quarters of South Africa's inhabitants are black, while one in seven (13 percent) are white.
CSS head Mark Orkin said that the largest proportion of unemployed blacks was found in the age category of 25 to 34 years.
"This may reflect the effects of uprisings against apartheid education particularly in the 1980s, which led to students not completing their education," he said.
Among black men and women only six percent had attained post-school qualifications compared to 30 percent of white men and 24 percent of white women.
On a gender basis, 23 percent of all males and 38 percent of women in South Africa were unemployed.

Black households were the poorest in the country where 26 percent had income ranging between zero and 6,839 rand a year. Whites also had the greatest share of the highest income jobs with 64 percent of white houseolds in this categtory compared with nine percent of African households.

The survey also found that of all South African employees, about one third belonged to a trade union. Membership was highest among black males at 39 percent, while white females were least likely to be members of trade unions at 17 percent.
